@Christopher Logan Thank you for drafting the options here, Chris! 

Avoiding truncation is an important part of the WCAG 2.2 compliance at the (baseline) Level A covered by the Success Criterion 1.4.4 Resize Text. It allows users with low vision to be able to access the same amount of information that other users would get, even when they are explicitly setting their own iOS settings to show larger fonts. 

Beyond providing an equal access to information, this is also something that is required for any accessibility compliance, either Section 508 in the US, EAA in EU, or the corresponding legal requirements enforced in India, Japan, Australia, etc. They all use WCAG 2.0 or 2.1, aiming to 2.2 for both Levels A and AA - and this criterion has been included even in the earlier versions of WCAG.

If we want to avoid stretching the titles for tiles on larger fonts, we could reflow the tiles section from 4 in a row to 3 and 2, or even 1 a row. This would still satisfy both the Resize Text and WCAG 2.2 Level AA SC 1.4.10 Reflow. While this appearance may not provide as compact view as it is on a "regular" font size, users who are proactively searching for larger font sizes are not expecting (and, per user feedback/research, do not like) those compact appearance because for them it means they would miss out on important information for something that is readily available for users with a better eyesight. These users are okay and expect and prefer to scroll the page. Oftentimes, users who find the content being cut or lost would choose an alternative application that does not limit their ability to access Internet independently.

To observe a user of screen magnification who is also relying on a large font size, I recommend to review the demo recorded by a Fable tester Carrie (on Android, but the same result and feedback would be on iOS device too) - the course and this video are available for any Mozillian with SSO, just use your SSO email to log in. 

There is a self-guided task in-progress with Fable for a user with iOS Magnification to do standard browsing actions with Firefox on iOS, it should be available by Tuesday, July 8th in the Fable platform. Also, an example of a feedback on the small UI size provided by a user relying on a large font size and, when needed, magnification that was recently shared in a Compatibility Test for Firefox iOS as well:
"The close button used to exit the carousel after reviewing all the  onboarding slides in Firefox was very small. The X to close the welcome slides, which highlight Firefox features after downloading the app, was difficult to locate. After reading all the slides, I had to magnify the screen just to find the close button, and even then, I had to keep the screen zoomed in to tap it accurately, as the touch target area was quite small. I recommend increasing the size of the close button to make it more perceivable and easier to interact with."

@Christopher Logan I think we could have the item 1 as:
* Name: [use on-screen string, i.e. Google Sponsored]
* Role: Button
* Note: use a hint to communicate the additional actions, i.e. "Double tap to remove, tap and hold to drag" (the iOS own home edit mode includes only the "tap and hold to drag", so the removal is not clear and not expected, so we could do better without making the navigation tedious)

And the 1a and 1b could be marked as "Presentational" so they are not expected to be focused separately. Basically, while we would ideally use `-` button as a separate control, because there may be multiple shortcuts on-screen available, users would have to navigate tediously twice to pass by each shortcut, and this would be more difficult. Since the removal is (expected to be) included in a tap action without a screen reader, double-tap with a screen reader would do it too. LMK if you have any questions

Item "4" that is a search field should have "Name: [use on-screen placeholder string]" and "Role: Search Field" - if you could add a "Note" in the annotation and provide a MagentA11y Search Field example link for engineers and QA folks to reference - this would be great. We'd expect VO to focus the field (excluding the google lens icon) and announce: "Search or enter address, Search field"
5. Item "4c" should be "5" because it would be a separate focusable element: it is a button, but @Christopher Logan we have to give it a human-redable, informative name, i.e. "Name: Use Google Lens to search" or similar - we need to provide an action that user would do if this button is activated

@Christopher Logan here we could use the "Role: list/group" and "Name: Shortcuts", so when a VoiceOver user focuses the first item in the list, they hear something like: "Shortcuts, [Google, sponsored], button" - similarly to the iOS Messages app when there are pinned items. The second and following buttons would not announce the label of the list anymore.

Also, we'd need items like "3a" for Google, "3b" for Amazon etc., i.e.
* 3a
* Name: "[use on-screen string], Sponsored"
* Role: button
then:
* 3b
* Name: "[use on-screen string], Sponsored"
* Role: button
